methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multi-institutional study of 1132 stage I NSCLC patients (2013-2021) with 57±37 month median follow-up. Inclusion criteria appropriately specify curative intent resection with lymph node dissection and minimum 36-month follow-up. Cox proportional hazards model used for multivariable analysis; variables with p<0.10 on univariate analysis included in multivariate model. However, STROBE reporting acknowledged but formal adherence assessment lacking. Potential unmeasured confounding regarding smoking-related comorbidities and performance status.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Cohort study identifying prognostic factors for recurrence in stage I NSCLC (pT>1a and non-lepidic adenocarcinoma subtypes predict worse DFS). Direct clinical relevance for postoperative risk stratification and adjuvant therapy decisions. However, observational design limits causal inference; identified associations may reflect underlying tumor biology rather than treatment-modifiable factors.

reporting_quality.justification: Explicitly adopts STROBE reporting guidelines; methods transparent regarding inclusion/exclusion criteria, patient characteristics, and statistical analyses. However, lacks pre-registration, conflict-of-interest disclosures, and explicit data availability statement. Center of treatment and calendar year included in sensitivity analyses, appropriately addressing temporal and institutional variability.

novelty_literature.justification: Confirms and extends prior observations regarding stage I NSCLC recurrence (Martini et al. 27% recurrence rate). Identifies histologic subtype (lepidic vs non-lepidic adenocarcinoma) as independent predictor in multivariable model, advancing beyond traditional pathological staging. However, pT staging and adenocarcinoma histotype associations with recurrence already recognized in literature.

writing_presentation.justification: Appropriately organized manuscript with clear methods, results, and discussion. Limitations section acknowledges retrospective design and potential unmeasured confounding. However, discussion could more thoroughly address mechanistic basis for lepidic subtype protection or compare findings to recent international guidelines (e.g., ESMO 2022 NSCLC recommendations).

key_strengths: Large multi-institutional cohort (n=1132) with adequate follow-up (57±37 months) capturing both early (32.1% within 12 months) and late recurrences
Identifies independent multivariable predictors: pT>1a (p=0.001) and non-lepidic adenocarcinoma (p<0.001) for recurrence risk stratification
Explicit STROBE reporting adopted; sensitivity analyses address institutional and temporal confounding
Detailed outcome data: distinguishes local (n=86) versus distant (n=138) recurrences with clinical implications for surveillance strategies
key_concerns: Observational retrospective design limits causal inference; unmeasured confounding regarding smoking-related comorbidities, pulmonary function, and genetic factors unaddressed
No propensity score matching or similar technique to balance baseline characteristics across surgical approaches/institutions
Adenocarcinoma histotype associations with recurrence already well-established in literature; incremental novelty limited
Discussion lacks detailed mechanistic explanation for lepidic subtype prognostic advantage beyond prior literature
No analysis of postoperative adjuvant therapy impact on recurrence patterns or survival
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically adequate retrospective prognostic study confirming known stage I NSCLC risk factors with solid follow-up data. Appropriate for Tier 4 journals; minor revisions should expand discussion of mechanistic basis for lepidic subtype protection.
